summary: This section stops large groups of people from starting a business to make a profit without registering as a company first. The law sets a maximum limit on how many members can join such an unregistered group. However, family businesses and certain professional partnerships are free from this rule.
points: Unregistered business groups must not exceed the prescribed member limit if their goal is to make a profit.
Such profit-seeking groups must register as a company under this Act or another law.
The prescribed member limit cannot be more than one hundred persons.
A Hindu undivided family carrying on business is exempt from this rule.
Professionals governed by special acts who form an association or partnership are exempt.
Every member in a violating business faces a fine up to one lakh rupees and personal liability for debts.
example: A group of one hundred and twenty friends in Mumbai decided to form an unregistered partnership named Apex Traders to buy and sell electronics for a profit. They did not register as a company under the Act or any other law, and they do not belong to a Hindu undivided family or governed professional bodies. Because their group size exceeds the legal limit allowed for unregistered profit-seeking associations, they are operating in violation of the law. Consequently, every member of Apex Traders faces a fine of up to one lakh rupees and becomes personally responsible for all the debts and liabilities the business incurs.

terms.meaning: A group of people working together for a common purpose.
A traditional family structure in India recognized for joint business and property ownership.
An action that breaks a law or rule.

watch: Do not confuse this rule with registered companies, as this section only restricts large unregistered profit-seeking groups.
